translation_en: Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not ask for leadership. If it is given to you because you asked for it, you will be left to manage it alone; if it is given without your asking, you will be helped in it.” This is the same chain through Shayban ibn Farrukh, Jarir ibn Hazim, al-Hasan, and Abd al-Rahman.

This is the same advice to Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah through Yahya ibn Yahya, Khalid ibn Abdullah, Yunus; Ali ibn Hujr through Hushaim, Yunus, Mansur, and Humayd; and Abu Kamil through Hammad ibn Zayd. All report it from al-Hasan. The chains are Yahya ibn Yahya from Khalid ibn Abdullah and Yunus; Ali ibn Hujr from Hushaim, Yunus, Mansur, and Humayd; and Abu Kamil from Hammad ibn Zayd, Simak ibn Atiyyah, Yunus ibn Ubayd, and Hisham ibn Hassan, all from al-Hasan and Abd al-Rahman ibn Samurah.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “Your oath is judged according to what your companion accepts as confirming it.” Amr’s version says, “what your companion confirms by it.” The chain is Yahya ibn Yahya and Amr al-Naqid, through Hushaim ibn Bashir and Abdullah ibn Abi Salih, from his father, and Abu Hurairah.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “The oath is according to the intention of the person who asks you to swear it.” Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “The oath is according to the intention of the person who asks you to swear it.” The chain is Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Yazid ibn Harun, Hushaim, Abbad ibn Abi Salih, his father, and Abu Hurairah.

Abu Hurairah reported that Solomon had sixty wives and said, “Tonight I will visit all of them, and each will conceive and bear a boy who will fight in the path of Allah.” None conceived except one, who gave birth to half a human being. The Messenger of Allah said, “Had he said, ‘If Allah wills,’ each would have borne a boy who would fight in the path of Allah.” The chain is Abu al-Rabi and Abu Kamil, from Hammad ibn Zayd, Ayyub, Muhammad, and Abu Hurairah.

Abu Hurairah reported that Solomon said he would visit seventy women that night, each of whom would bear a boy who would fight in the path of Allah. His companion, or an angel, told him to say, “If Allah wills,” but he forgot. Only one of his wives gave birth, and she delivered half a boy. The Messenger of Allah said, “Had he said, ‘If Allah wills,’ he would not have broken his oath, and it would have helped him achieve what he wanted.”
This is a similar report from Abu Hurairah through Ibn Abi Umar, Sufyan, Abu al-Zinad, and al-Araj. This is the same account from Abu Hurairah through Ibn Abi Umar, Sufyan, Abu al-Zinad, and al-Araj.

Abu Hurairah reported that Solomon said he would visit seventy women that night, each bearing a boy who would fight in the path of Allah. He was told to say, “If Allah wills,” but he did not. Only one woman gave birth to half a human being. The Messenger of Allah said that if Solomon had said it, he would not have broken his oath and would have achieved his aim. Abd ibn Humayd transmitted this through Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, Ibn Tawus, his father, and Abu Hurairah, with the same report about Solomon and the women.

Abu Hurairah reported that Solomon said he would visit ninety women, each bearing a horseman who would fight in the path of Allah. His companion told him to say, “If Allah wills,” but he did not. Only one woman conceived, and she gave birth to half a man. The Prophet said that had Solomon said it, they all would have fought in Allah’s path as horsemen. Abu Hurairah reported that Solomon said he would visit ninety women and each would bear a horseman to fight in Allah’s path. His companion told him to say, “If Allah wills,” but Solomon did not. He visited them all, but only one conceived and gave birth to half a man. The Prophet swore by Him who holds Muhammad’s soul that if Solomon had said it, they all would have fought in Allah’s path as horsemen. The chain is Zuhayr ibn Harb, Shababah, Warqa, Abu al-Zinad, and al-Araj.
This is the same report through Suwayd ibn Said, Hafs ibn Maysarah, and Musa ibn Uqbah, from Abu al-Zinad, with the wording that each woman would conceive a boy who would strive in Allah’s path.

Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “By Allah, for one of you to persist in an oath against his family is more sinful before Allah than giving the expiation that Allah has prescribed.” Abu Hurairah reported that the Messenger of Allah said: “By Allah, for one of you to persist in an oath against his family is more sinful before Allah than giving the expiation Allah has prescribed.” The transmitters are Muhammad ibn Rafi, Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, and Hammam ibn Munabbih.

Ibn Umar reported that Umar said to the Messenger of Allah: “In the pre-Islamic period, I vowed to spend a night in retreat at the Sacred Mosque.” The Messenger said, “Fulfill your vow.” Umar said to the Messenger of Allah: “In the pre-Islamic period, I vowed to spend a night in retreat at the Sacred Mosque.” The Messenger replied, “Fulfill your vow.” It is reported by Muhammad ibn Abi Bakr, Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, and Zuhayr ibn Harb from Yahya al-Qattan, Ubayd Allah, Nafi, and Ibn Umar.

This is the same report through several chains from Ubayd Allah, Nafi, and Ibn Umar. Abu Usamah’s and al-Thaqafi’s versions say Umar vowed to spend a night in retreat; Shubah’s says he vowed to spend a day. Hafs does not specify a day or night. This report has several chains from Ubayd Allah, Nafi, and Ibn Umar. Abu Usamah and Abd al-Wahhab al-Thaqafi say Umar vowed one night of retreat; Shubah says he vowed one day. Hafs ibn Ghiyath reports it from Umar and does not specify day or night. Other transmitters include Abu Said al-Ashajj, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Muhammad ibn al-Ala, Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Abu Usamah, and Muhammad ibn Jafar.

Ibn Umar said Umar asked the Messenger of Allah at al-Ji‘ranah, after returning from al-Taif, about a pre-Islamic vow to spend one day in retreat at the Sacred Mosque. The Messenger said, “Go and spend a day in retreat.” Umar had received a servant girl from the fifth of the spoils. When the Messenger freed the captives, Umar heard them say he had freed them. Umar told Abdullah to go and release that servant girl too. Umar asked the Messenger at al-Ji‘ranah, after returning from al-Taif, how to fulfill a pre-Islamic vow to spend one day in retreat at the Sacred Mosque. The Messenger said, “Go and spend a day in retreat.” Umar had received a servant girl from the fifth of the spoils. When the Messenger freed the captives, Umar heard them say they had been freed. Umar then told his son Abdullah to go and release that servant girl. The chain is Abu Tahir, Ibn Wahb, Jarir ibn Hazim, Ayyub, Nafi, Ibn Umar, and Umar.

Ibn Umar said that when the Prophet returned from Hunayn, Umar asked about a vow he had made in the pre-Islamic period to spend one day in retreat. This is similar to Jarir ibn Hazim’s report. Ibn Umar said that after the Prophet returned from Hunayn, Umar asked him about his pre-Islamic vow to spend one day in retreat. This is similar to Jarir ibn Hazim’s report and is transmitted through Abd ibn Humayd, Abd al-Razzaq, Maamar, Ayyub, and Nafi.

Nafi said that when Ibn Umar was told about the Messenger’s minor pilgrimage from al-Ji‘ranah, he said the Messenger had not performed one from there. Nafi added that Umar had vowed in the pre-Islamic period to spend a night in retreat. This is similar to the reports of Jarir ibn Hazim and Maamar from Ayyub.

This is the same report from Ibn Umar through Hammad and through Abd al-Ala and Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Both versions say that Umar’s vow was to spend one day in retreat. This report is from Ibn Umar through two chains: Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Darimi, Hajjaj ibn al-Minhal, and Hammad; and Yahya ibn Khalaf, Abd al-Ala, and Muhammad ibn Ishaq. Both versions state that Umar vowed one day of retreat.

Zadhan Abu Umar said he went to Ibn Umar after Ibn Umar had freed a slave. Ibn Umar picked up a small piece of earth and said, “There is no reward in this worth even this, except that I heard the Messenger of Allah say: ‘Whoever slaps or strikes his slave, his expiation is to set him free.’”

Ibn Umar called one of his young slaves and saw a mark on his back. He asked whether he had hurt him. The slave said no, and Ibn Umar said, “You are free.” He then picked up something from the ground and said, “I have no reward worth even this,” for he had heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever strikes a slave without a lawful punishment, or slaps him, must set him free.”

This is the same report through Waki and Abd al-Rahman, both from Sufyan and Firas. Ibn Mahdi’s version includes “without a lawful punishment”; Waki’s says “whoever slaps his slave” and omits that phrase. This is the same report through Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Waki and Abd al-Rahman, both from Sufyan and Firas. Ibn Mahdi’s version includes “without a lawful punishment”; Waki’s wording is “whoever slaps his slave” and does not mention the punishment.

Muawiyah ibn Suwayd said: “I slapped a servant of ours and ran away. I returned shortly before noon and prayed behind my father. He called the servant and me, then told me to let the servant retaliate. The servant forgave me. My father said, ‘We, the Banu Muqarrin, had only one servant in the time of the Messenger of Allah. One of us slapped her, and the Prophet was told. He said, “Set her free.”’ They said they had no other servant. He said, ‘Then use her until you can do without her, and then let her go.’”

HIlal ibn Yasaf said an older man slapped his servant. Suwayd ibn Muqarrin said, “Could you find no one else but her face?” He said that he was the seventh of seven brothers of Banu Muqarrin, and they had only one servant. The youngest slapped her, so the Messenger of Allah ordered them to set her free.

HIlal ibn Yasaf said they were selling cloth in the house of Suwayd ibn Muqarrin, brother of al-Numan ibn Muqarrin. A servant girl came out and said something to one of the men, who slapped her. Suwayd became angry and related a story like Ibn Idris’s report.

Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir asked Shubah his name, then told him that Abu Shubah al-Iraqi reported from Suwayd ibn Muqarrin that someone slapped his servant girl. Suwayd asked whether he knew that striking the face was forbidden. He said he had been one of seven brothers with the Messenger of Allah, and they had only one servant. One of them slapped her, so the Messenger ordered them to free her.

This is the same account through Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna from Wahb ibn Jarir and Shubah. This is the same account as Abd al-Samad’s report, transmitted by Ishaq ibn Ibrahim and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna through Wahb ibn Jarir and Shubah.

Abu Masud al-Badri said: “I was whipping a young slave of mine when I heard a voice behind me saying, ‘Know, Abu Masud!’ I was so angry that I did not understand the voice. As it came closer, I saw it was the Messenger of Allah, who repeated, ‘Know, Abu Masud, know, Abu Masud!’ I dropped the whip. He said, ‘Know, Abu Masud, Allah has more power over you than you have over this boy.’ I said, ‘I will never strike a slave again.’” Abu Masud al-Badri said he was whipping one of his young slaves when he heard a voice behind him say, “Know, Abu Masud!” In his anger he did not recognize the voice. When the speaker came near, he saw the Messenger of Allah, who repeated, “Know, Abu Masud!” Abu Masud dropped the whip. The Prophet said, “Know, Abu Masud, Allah has more power over you than you have over this boy.” Abu Masud replied, “I will never strike a slave again.” The chain includes Abu Kamil al-Jahdari, Abd al-Wahid ibn Ziyad, al-Amash, Ibrahim al-Taymi, and his father.

This is the same account through several chains from al-Amash, through Ibrahim al-Taymi and his father, from Abu Masud. Jarir’s version adds that the whip fell from his hand out of awe of the Prophet. This is the same account through other chains from al-Amash with the chain of Abd al-Wahid. Jarir’s version says the whip fell from Abu Masud’s hand out of awe of the Prophet. Other transmitters include Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, Zuhayr ibn Harb, Muhammad ibn Humayd, Sufyan, Muhammad ibn Rafi, Abd al-Razzaq, Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Affan, and Abu Awanah.

Abu Masud al-Ansari said: “I was striking a slave when I heard a voice behind me saying, ‘Know, Abu Masud, Allah has more power over you than you have over him.’ I turned and saw the Messenger of Allah. I said, ‘Messenger of Allah, he is free for Allah’s sake.’ The Prophet said, ‘Had you not done that, the Fire would have scorched you, or touched you.’”

Abu Masud used to strike his servant, who kept saying, “I seek refuge in Allah.” He continued striking him until the servant said, “I seek refuge in the Messenger of Allah.” Then he stopped. The Messenger said, “By Allah, Allah has more power over you than you have over him.” Abu Masud then freed the servant.

This is the same report through Bishr ibn Khalid and Muhammad ibn Jafar from Shubah, with the same chain, but it omits the servant saying, “I seek refuge in Allah; I seek refuge in the Messenger of Allah.”
